Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the revision, including the Annexures attached therewith.

2. This criminal revision under Section 397/401 CrPC has been filed against the judgment and order dated 21st February, 2014 passed by the Additional District and Sessions Judge, Court No. 4,
Faizabad (Ayodhya) in Criminal Appeal No. 26 of 2013 'Ram Bahadur Vs. State of U.P.' preferred by the revisionist against the order dated 4the February, 2013 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-1, Court No. 10, Faizabad (Ayodhya) in Criminal Complaint No.565 of 2007 under Section 7/16 The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 lodged at Police Station Cantt., District Faizabad (Ayodhya) whereby the revisionist was convicted under Section 7/16 The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as the 'PFA Act,') and sentenced six months rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,000/-, and in the event of non-payment of fine, seven days additional imprisonment.

sentences.text: 3. The appellate Court has dismissed the appeal vide the impugned judgment and order dated 21st February, 2014 and affirmed the judgment of conviction and fine passed by the learned trial Court.
4. The revisionist is a milkman, whose milk was taken for testing on 22nd May, 2006 by the Food Inspector.

The Public Analyst, in his report dated 26th June, 2006, opined that the milk fat was was 5.3% and milk solids-not-fat was 7.1% and, thus, it was opined that the milk solids-not-fat was 16%
less than the prescribed limit.
The Central Food Laboratory also examined the sample, which was sent to it on request of the revisionist.

The report of the Central Food Laboratory dated 2nd March,
2010 has been placed on record.
According to the said report, the milk fat was 6%, and it was above the prescribed limit of 4.5%, however, the milk solids-not-fat was found to be 6.1%, which is less than 8.5%.

5. Counsel for the revisionist submits that the milk fat was not injurious to human health; only the milk solids-not-fat was less than the prescribed limit inasmuch as in the report of Public Analyst it was found 7.1%, and it was less than the standard limit of 8.5%.
The learned counsel further submits that the incident took place around 14 years before; the revisionist has undergone around 35 days imprisonment.

The learned counsel places reliance on judgment in 'Sughar Singh Vs. State and another' (Criminal Revision No.985 of 1991) in which this Court, after considering the facts of the case, which are identical to the present one, found the offence to be of very minor nature.

entities.text: Sughar Singh Vs. State and another' (Criminal Revision No.985 of 1991)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The milk solids-not-fat was not injurious to the health.

6. The Supreme Court in Nand Lal v. State of Uttarakhand and others, 2010 (4) SCC 562, after considering the age of the appellant in that case, and taking into account the fact that the incident was very old, reduced the sentence to the period already undergone.

entities.text: Nand Lal v. State of Uttarakhand and others, 2010 (4) SCC 562
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the said judgment of the Supreme Court, and trivial nature of the offence committed by the revisionist, it would be appropriate to reduce the sentence to the sentence already undergone by the revisionist with enhanced fine.

8. In view thereof, the sentence awarded to the revisionist is reduced to the sentence already undergone by him with fine of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees five thousand) to be deposited by the revisionist with the trial Court within a period of four weeks from today.
9. Thus, the revision is allowed partly.

10. Let copy of this order, along with lower court record, be sent to the concerned Court below forthwith for compliance.
[D.K. Singh, J.]
